Impacts on animals will occur both in the United States and worldwide.

The total animal impacts, however, will be more pronounced with populations in the United States. Here species will more directly benefit from protection and management provided by the proposed legislation. Essential actions can be identified and effectively carried out on the same level (State or Federal) of government. Endangered species in other countries can also be benefitted by the United States government through:
1. Bilateral agreement.
2. Training of foreign nationals in wildlife management.
3. Technical advice in wildlife management problems.
4. Removal of the U.S. market from the economic demand for foreign endangered wildlife.
5. Cooperation with other governments in the context of the Treaty which has been developed to provide for control of trade in all threatened species.
All of the above have been provided in current authority. Results of the measures and impact of the action on animals will depend upon (1) our skill in negotiating agreements with other countries and (2) the U.S. proportion of the total world demand for endangered animal products.
